title: Escort
text: Before long, the envoy from Siltvelt joined us.
“Does this prove we can be trusted?”
“Excuse me.”
I activated the slave mark without warning. The envoy in front of me immediately clutched his chest and groaned. I canceled the command right away and nodded.
“It seems you weren’t lying after all.”
“Y-yes. Hah… hah…”
“Now, I have a few questions for you. If you lie, I’ll kill you on the spot.”
“I-it’s okay!”
I asked every question I could think of—such as whether he had any other allies or if he was plotting to kill my Father—but he showed no reaction. It seems he really is on our side.
“M-Motoyasu, isn’t that a bit rude to do that out of the blue?”
“Better safe than sorry. But the fact remains that this proves he can’t betray us… Please guide us to Siltvelt.”

The messenger saluted at my words. If he shows this much sincerity and loyalty, perhaps I can trust him. Going so far as to become a slave just to earn someone’s trust… If I could become a slave too, I’d love to be Filo-tan’s slave! No… I was The Love Hunter, and at the same time, a Slave of Love. HAHAHA.
“So, Lord Kitamura, regarding whether or not to level up Lord Iwatani…”
“Ah, I’d like to speak on that very matter.”
The messenger raised his hand to speak. True to his Demi-Human nature, his animal-like ears were twitching up and down. It reminds me of the slaves in Father’s village.
“What is it?”
“The Queen of Melromarc has requested that the wanted notice be withdrawn, so I believe it will be removed shortly.”

Hmm… So this is what my Father meant when he said she was trustworthy. The Queen has a deeper understanding of the situation. To me, she looks like nothing more than a pig, but when it comes to my Finacée’s parents… perhaps there’s something to it. For now, I suppose it’s safe to classify her as an ally.
“So if I hide for a few days, I’ll be able to walk around freely?”
“Well…”

Éclair’s eyes darted around at Father’s words. It’s a tricky problem, isn’t it? Even if adventurers and bounty hunters stop targeting me, the Three Heroes Church members will likely remain the same. And since the majority of Melromarc soldiers are Three Heroes Church members, even the soldiers themselves are dangerous.
“Even if the warrant is lifted, there’s still a high chance assassins will come after you, so you should be careful.”

Come to think of it, I can’t help but wonder how my father managed to survive before the loop began. To rise to prominence in a situation like this… He really must be exceptionally talented. Could it be because of the various events that occurred on the very first day when I showed up? Perhaps the Three Heroes Church viewed my father as insignificant and assumed he’d just die out in the wilderness…?

For the first month, my Father was wearing some pretty shoddy gear. Big Sister wasn’t that strong either… I remember I was over Level 40 back then… around 47, if I recall correctly. Since my Father was strong enough back then to pin me down and corner me, I wonder just how strong he really was?

…I’d like to guess Level 30, but knowing my Father—who paid close attention to even the smallest details of his stats—he might have been around Level 20. Heroes and their companions receive an EXP bonus. From the perspective of an ordinary adventurer, the Three Heroes Church might have viewed us as mere fodder—around Level 10 or so. If that’s the case, it’s not impossible to imagine they ignored us as insignificant… and waited until other heroes had grown stronger.
“What level are you all, by the way?”
“…Sorry. We just happened to be staying nearby, so we’re not that strong. I’m level 35, and the other two are 29 and 28.”

That’s a bit of a worrying level range, isn’t it? I don’t know what level Éclair is, but she’s probably around 60 at most. My Father is level 1, so it’s difficult to take him to dangerous places. I’d have to stay close by to do power-leveling like we did on the last run… and if we got ambushed while I was away, it’d be a disaster.
To break out of this “hardcore play” situation, our only option is to flee to a place beyond the Three Heroes Church’s reach. Ah, I miss Filolial-sama.
“It’d be great if there were a place we could hide…”
Éclair turns her gaze toward the messenger.
“Given the waves, places around here where we could hide…”
“The former territory my father used to manage…? That’ll be tough.”
Hiding is difficult, too. Hiding in a mountain cabin or something is an option, but it’s a tough proposition.
“For now, our top priority should be getting out of this country.”
“Yeah… I thought this would be a dream-like adventure in another world, but it’s turned out to be a total disaster.”

My father grumbles. I can understand how he feels. When I first came to this other world, all I could think about was pigs. Looking back on my own foolishness now, I feel like I could cry blood. My Father managed to rise above such unpleasant feelings. This time, I, Motoyasu, will be helping out, so things might go better than last time.
“Understood. The road with less foot traffic is this way.”
And so, while escorting my Father, our journey continues.

The next day, a messenger from Siltvelt who had gone to confirm that the wanted poster had been removed informed us of this. Right now, Father is cooking the meat from the monster we defeated yesterday.
“Whoa! So, are you really sure it’s okay for me to cook this? I’m not that good at it, you know.”
“Father, there’s no need to be so modest.”
“That’s true. Mr. Iwatani is quite the cook.”
“Yes. As expected of the Shield Hero.”
“Oink oink.”
“Oooh.”
It seems even the Demi-Human sow is enjoying the taste.
“I wonder if that’s true?”

Saying that, my Father uses the sword he borrowed from Éclair as a kitchen knife and begins cutting up the meat. I’ve noticed, you know. He’s casually cutting through the meat’s sinews to make it easier to eat and scoring it to help the heat penetrate better. My Father, who even drains the blood without even thinking about it, has a natural talent for cooking. What’s more, he’s wrapped the leftover meat in a bag and placed it in the corner of the wagon to let it tenderize, all to enhance the flavor. He even uses the bones to make broth without wasting a single bit, so there’s no way I could say it tastes bad.
“Oh, I think it would taste even better if we had some herbs or something? There’s still a bit of a gamey smell…”
“What? It’s going to get even better than this?”
Éclair looks surprised. The messenger is also glancing around, searching for wild herbs.
“Anyway… to get to Siltvelt, we’ll need to cross the border. If the wanted poster has disappeared, we can assume there won’t be much of a problem.”

Once everyone has finished eating, Éclair unfolds a map and checks it in front of the group. …That’s exactly where the problem lies. Last time, we saw my father off, and two days later, we confirmed he had died. Judging by the map, it seems he must have been approaching the border around that time. So, if anything is going on, it would likely be around then. We can’t completely rule out the possibility that the Siltvelt envoy is actually… something else, so we’re keeping a close eye on things.
“It’s too soon to jump to conclusions. We’d better stay on high alert.”
“True, but…”
“We should be especially vigilant along the border. They might be gathering there.”
“Hmm…”

Éclair seems to be thinking it over as well. We were once deceived by Kuzvich and the Three Heroes Church and ended up tracking Father. I remember there were a great many of them gathered at the fortress back then. This time, since it’s only been a few days since they were summoned, there’s likely a limit to how many they can muster, but it’s highly probable they’re on high alert.
“There’s the option of taking the mountain trail instead of passing through the border fortress… but if security measures are in place, it’s pointless. It’d just hinder our progress.”
“That’s true. It might be difficult if we can’t escape.”
“No, if it’s just a matter of escaping, I think Lord Kitamura’s teleportation ability could handle it.”
“In that case, don’t we have no choice but to go? If we fail, we can just run away.”
“I can’t say that for certain.”
“Huh? Is that so?”
It seems my father and Éclair have misunderstood something. There’s a problem with the teleportation skill.
“This is a story from the future, but there was a time when Ren and Itsuki were nearly eliminated by the Three Heroes Church when they went rogue. Do you know why they couldn’t escape back then?”
“I don’t know…? Are there restrictions on the teleportation skill?”

I nod in agreement with my father’s words. That’s right—the portal skill has several limitations. I believe Father discovered these through his own experiments. When you think about it, it’s quite a twist of fate.

“You have to program the destination into the skill’s memory. Generally, you can’t do that inside a building. And if you try to use it in an area protected by a barrier, you won’t be able to teleport.”
“A barrier…?”

“Specifically, places like dragon habitats. Other examples include areas where Filolial-sama or certain monsters assert their territories… and in human settlements, the vicinity of churches also falls under this category. Additionally, regions where waves are active are included as well.”
“Huh… and what does that have to do with escaping?”
“Why do you think Ren and Itsuki weren’t able to escape? There’s more to it than that.”
“Weren’t they caught off guard and didn’t even have time to use it?”
“While I can’t rule out that possibility, I’ve confirmed that it can’t be used even within the range where Ceremonial Magic is being cast.”

Actually, when I was attacked by the Pope, I instinctively cast Portal Spear. Foolishly, I tried to protect the Crimson Swine Bitch and the other pigs. At the time, I wondered why it wouldn’t work, but subsequent experiments revealed that it can’t be used while under the effect of Ceremonial Magic.
“Ceremonial Magic?”
“It’s a type of Magic often used in war. I see—if they were serious about killing Lord Iwatani and Lord Kitamura, it would make perfect sense to use it.”
“If they cast the Ceremonial Magic ‘Sanctuary,’ you can consider it impossible to escape.”

Sanctuary is Magic with properties similar to a barrier Magic, capable of dispelling most negative attacks and curses. Since it persists for a while, escaping via teleportation would indeed be impossible.
“Then what should we do…?”
“That’s exactly where I come in. With my power alone, I believe I can handle just about anything.”
“So it’s just brute force after all. I thought you might have some secret strategy.”
“The direct approach is the most efficient, you know.”
“‘Sigh…’”
For some reason, Éclair and my father both let out deep sighs. It seems they’ve become close without me even noticing. To forge such a bond with someone in such a short time—that’s my father for you.
“Well then, let’s try going head-on for now. If anything happens, I’ll count on you, Motoyasu-kun.”
“Leave it to me.”
And so, our journey toward Siltvelt continues.
